html:
SMTO-EXE-0235 — SMTO couldn't finish downloading the Docker image

GUID: 935a8ed8-9906-5796-a911-d7f12456c796
Slug: docker-pull-failed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The image download started on the Gateway computer but did not finish successfully. Part of the image may already be saved there, but SMTO can't confirm the complete image arrived.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to list the Docker images on that Gateway and look for the image you wanted. If the image already arrived, you don't need to download it again.
  2. Check that the image name and version tag are spelled exactly as shown on the registry's website, for example nginx:1.27. A misspelled name or a tag that doesn't exist is a common reason a download fails partway.
  3. Make sure the computer running the Gateway is switched on and can reach the internet or your company's image registry. The Gateway downloads the image itself, so it needs its own working connection to the registry.
  4. After fixing the cause, ask SMTO to download the image again, and approve the request if SMTO asks. SMTO never repeats a Docker download on its own; a new request starts a fresh, checked download.

What success looks like

  • The image appears in the list of Docker images on that Gateway with the name and tag you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Open Technical details in this panel, select Copy error details, and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't delete partly downloaded images by hand while you wait; the next download can reuse them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Docker image pull (or Compose pull) on the selected Gateway reported failure after the transfer had started, and a read-only check could not confirm the image arrived; some layers or tags may already be present.

What this means

  • After mutation began, an image/Compose pull reported operation failure and existing reconciliation did not establish success. Some image layers or tags may already exist. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • After mutation began, an image/Compose pull reported operation failure and existing reconciliation did not establish success. Some image layers or tags may already exist.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact image reference, bounded progress and current Engine image state.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the requested reference with docker.images / docker.image on the selected Gateway and read the Engine's pull error (for example journalctl -u docker on that host). Correct the cause (image name/tag, registry reachability, registry credentials) and submit a new docker.image_pull; pulling by immutable digest lets SMTO confirm the result.
  • Inspect current image state and the reported pull cause before a new authorized request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • Original pull effects are reconciled and any required continued acquisition produces the intended verified image.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
